Pricing

What Google Ads freelancers and PPC consultants actually charge

The three ways this industry charges and where each one quietly works against you, what the market typically costs, and how I price audits, management and consulting.

Get a quoteView services & pricing

The three models, and the catch in each

Percentage of ad spend

Typically 10% to 20% of monthly spend, often with a minimum. Easy to understand, and the incentive runs backwards: the consultant earns more when you spend more, not when you spend better. Watch what happens when the honest advice is to cut budget.

Flat monthly retainer

A fixed fee regardless of spend. Incentives are cleaner and budgeting is predictable. The risk is scope: if landing pages, tracking or reporting sit outside the retainer, the recommendations you need most never get implemented.

Hourly

Rates vary enormously with seniority and market. Fine for audits and advisory. Bad for ongoing management, because you start hesitating before asking a question, which is exactly when accounts drift.

The number nobody quotes: whatever the model, ask what happens to the account if you leave. If the campaigns, conversion actions and tags live in the vendor's accounts rather than yours, the real price is that you cannot go.

What freelance Google Ads management typically costs

Ranges observed across the US and UK markets, for context rather than as a quote. Freelancer rates cluster lower than agency rates for the same spend because there is no account manager, office or margin stack in between; senior freelancers sit at the top of the freelance range and overlap with small agencies.

Monthly ad spendFreelance specialistSmall agencyNotes
Under $3,000One-off setup or auditUsually below minimumsA retainer rarely makes sense here
$3,000 – $10,000Flat retainer, low four figuresMinimum retainer or 15–20% of spendWhere the freelance model is strongest
$10,000 – $50,000Flat retainer, scaled by scope10–15% of spendPercentage models start to overcharge here
Over $50,000Flat retainer, fractional leadCustom, often 8–12% ($4,000–6,000+)Structure and measurement matter more than bids

Hourly consulting from senior practitioners runs from roughly $100 to $300 an hour depending on market; freelance marketplaces list much lower rates, mostly from people early in their careers or in lower-cost regions.

How I price

Every engagement is quoted from the form, in US dollars, pounds or euros, because the scope decides the number: monthly spend, number of platforms and markets, and whether tracking has to be rebuilt. What you can rely on before the call is the model.

EngagementModelWhat is included
Google Ads auditFixed price, quoted up frontWritten report, fixes ranked by impact, walkthrough call. Credited against the first month of management.
Management, up to ~$10K/month spendFlat monthly feeWeekly work, tracking maintained, landing page fixes, written monthly report. Month to month.
Management, $10K to $50K/month spendFlat monthly fee, scaled by scopeSame scope with more campaigns, markets or platforms.
Management, over $50K/month spendFlat monthly fee, quoted per accountMultiple platforms and markets, weekly call, a fractional head of paid media rather than an operator.
Account setupFixed priceStructure, ads, negatives, tracking, launch and handover document.
Conversion tracking rebuildFixed priceGA4, Tag Manager, enhanced and offline conversions, reconciliation report.
Consulting and advisoryHourly, or fixed price per deliverableStrategy, second opinions and standing sessions with in-house teams.
White label, per client accountFlat monthly fee per accountVolume pricing for several accounts. Your brand, your template.

None of these is a percentage of ad spend, so the advice to cut budget costs me nothing to give. Adding Microsoft Advertising to a Google retainer is a small increase; adding Meta with weekly creative testing is a larger one, agreed up front. The form asks for exactly that and you get a range back the same day; a firm number needs a look at the account.

What is not in the price

Ad spend is paid by you, directly to Google, Microsoft, Meta or LinkedIn, from your own billing profile. Paid tools beyond what the platforms provide are rare and agreed first. Creative production at volume, for Meta-heavy accounts, is done with your designer or a studio and billed by them. Everything else that the account needs to perform, including tracking fixes and landing page changes I can make myself, is inside the retainer.

Questions people ask before hiring

Why not charge a percentage of ad spend like most agencies?

Because it pays the consultant to grow spend rather than results. A flat fee removes that conflict. When the right advice is to cut budget, I can give it without cutting my own income.

Is there a setup fee?

No separate setup fee. New accounts start with the audit, which is a fixed price and is credited against the first month of management.

Is there a minimum contract length?

No. Management is month to month with a notice period. Accounts need a few months to show what a change did, and most clients stay well beyond that, but the choice is theirs each month.

Do you charge more for multiple platforms?

Scope, not platform count, sets the fee. Adding Microsoft Advertising to a Google Ads account is a small increase; adding Meta with weekly creative testing is a larger one. It is agreed up front and revisited when scope changes.

Can I get a quote without a call?

Yes. The form asks for monthly spend, platforms and what you are trying to fix, and a range comes back by email. A firm price needs a look at the account, which is a short call or read-only access.

What if I only want a one-off fix, not management?

That is the audit, or a fixed-price project such as a setup or a tracking rebuild. Many engagements are exactly that and never become retainers.
